subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should LaunchAgent-managed raw-stream logging fail closed when an operator sets `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0` or unsets it via `launchctl`, even if a generated service env file or config env source still contains `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=1`?
rationale: This changes precedence for sensitive diagnostic logging across launchd inherited env, generated service env files, state-dir `.env`, and config env; automation should not choose that security boundary silently.

options.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
options.body: Treat an explicit operator false/unset path as disabling raw-stream writes and add Doctor/status/docs proof for hidden service-env cleanup.

options.title: Document Durable Source Precedence
options.body: Keep durable service env/config values authoritative but make Doctor/status identify the active source and document how to remove it.

options.title: Require Maintainer Repro First
options.body: Hold implementation until a macOS LaunchAgent live repro captures the process env, generated service env file, and append behavior in one trace.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
recommendation.body: Treat an explicit operator false/unset path as disabling raw-stream writes and add Doctor/status/docs proof for hidden service-env cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation and docs for the affected paths are carried by Peter Steinberger's recent current-main commit.
